t:
(a) Resumption of Authority to Authorize Transitional Use.—Subsection (a) of section 1147 of title 10, United States Code, is amended—
        (1) in paragraph (1), by striking “October 1, 1990, and ending on December 31, 2001” and inserting “October 1, 2012, and ending on December 31, 2018”; and 
        (2) in paragraph (2), by striking “October 1, 1994, and ending on December 31, 2001” and inserting “October 1, 2012, and ending on December 31, 2018”.  
    (b) Prohibition on Provision of Transitional Basic Allowance for Housing.—Such section is further amended by adding at the end the following new subsection:“(c) No Transitional Basic Allowance for Housing.—Nothing in this section shall be construed to authorize the Secretary concerned to continue to provide for any period of time to an individual who is involuntarily separated all or any portion of a basic allowance for housing to which the individual was entitled under section 403 of title 37 immediately before being involuntarily separated, even in cases in which the individual or members of the individual’s household continue to reside after the separation in a housing unit acquired or constructed under the alternative authority of subchapter IV of chapter 169 of this title that is not owned or leased by the United States.”. 
    (c) Correction of Reference to Administering Secretary.—Subsection (a)(2) of such section is further amended by striking “The Secretary of Transportation” and inserting “The Secretary concerned”.

fable.w: The section only extends the date ranges for transitional housing use, bars a transitional housing allowance, and corrects a reference to the administering Secretary. The tempting reading is that resuming an 'authority to authorize' implies rulemaking, but the text itself requires no regulation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, or consultation with any party outside the federal government. It also grants no outside party a right to sue or object.
fable.s: Nothing in this section shall be construed to authorize the Secretary concerned to continue to provide for any period of time to an individual who is involuntarily separated all or any portion of a basic allowance for housing

qwen_block.w: This section amends statutory dates and clarifies that the Secretary cannot provide housing allowances to involuntarily separated individuals. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties in the decision-making process. The interaction described is a benefit determination (which is explicitly excluded) and internal administrative authority.
qwen_block.s: Nothing in this section shall be construed to authorize the Secretary concerned to continue to provide for any period of time to an individual who is involuntarily separated all or any portion of a basic allowance for housing

opus.w: The section revives the authority to let involuntarily separated service members keep using military housing for a transition period, bans a transitional housing allowance, and changes a reference from one Secretary to another. No one outside the federal government is consulted or given a role in any decision. The mention of housing not owned or leased by the United States only defines which units the rule covers. It does not set up any consultation with private developers or any other outside party.
opus.s: a housing unit acquired or constructed under the alternative authority of subchapter IV of chapter 169 of this title that is not owned or leased by the United States
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through.** One tempting reading is that the mention of housing "acquired or constructed under the alternative authority of subchapter IV of chapter 169 ... that is not owned or leased by the United States" brings private housing developers into the decision. It doesn't. That clause only defines which housing units the ban on a transitional housing allowance covers. No private party is consulted. The changes to the dates and to which Secretary is responsible also stay entirely inside the federal government. There is no rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section amends dates for transitional housing authority and prohibits the provision of transitional basic allowance for housing to involuntarily separated individuals. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation by parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or experts) in the decision-making process. The changes are purely administrative and substantive regarding benefit eligibility, not procedural participation.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the prohibition on providing housing allowances affects individuals outside the government, thus involving them. However, this is a substantive rule change regarding benefits, not a procedural requirement for outside parties to participate in the decision-making process. The text contains no mechanisms for consultation, comment, hearings, or advisory input from non-federal entities.
